The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the story, the central tension is the quiet, unspoken romantic pull between Marian and Anton, constrained by the temporary nature of their residency and the fact that Anton has a wife in Rotterdam. The narrative builds toward their final outing together, reaching a near-climax on the beach when they almost give in to their feelings after escaping the rising tide. 

When the moment passes unacted upon, the story doesn't just abruptly stop; it resolves the emotional arc during the quiet drive back. The imagery of the tide erasing their footprints mirrors the ephemeral nature of their connection, while Marian's flash-forward to keeping the shells and Anton simply wanting to say her name one more time provide a deeply poignant sense of closure. It brings the characters to the exact emotional destination the entire piece had been leading toward: a tender, bittersweet acceptance of a connection that will remain unconsummated but fondly remembered.
